title: Arithmetic sequences
competency: Find the common difference, the nth term and arithmetic means of an arithmetic sequence.

keywords.def: A sequence where each term is the previous term plus a fixed number.
The fixed number d added each time: d = next term − this term.
The rule aₙ that gives the nth term.
A term between two given terms of an arithmetic sequence.

en.text: In an arithmetic sequence you add the same number every time. That fixed number is the common difference d = next term − this term. It can be positive, negative or a fraction.

am.text: በአሪትሜቲክ ቅደም ተከተል በየጊዜው አንድ አይነት ቁጥር እንደምራለን። ይህ ቋሚ ቁጥር የጋራ ልዩነት d ይባላል፤ d = ቀጣዩ ተርም − ይህ ተርም።

screens.title: Spot the jump
screens.ask: What is added each time in 3, 7, 11, 15, …?
screens.after:
Subtract each term from the next: 7 − 3 = 4, 11 − 7 = 4, 15 − 11 = 4.
The same jump, 4, each time.
(3 is the first term, not the jump.)

screens.title: Find the difference
items: Difference 1/3: 2 = 6/3 and 3 = 9/3, so each step adds 1/3.

screens.title: Hop along 3, 7, 11, 15
screens.ask: Tap ▶ to hop. Each hop adds the same number.
screens.after: Every hop is +4. The fixed jump is the common difference: d = 4.

screens.title: Arithmetic sequence
paras: Each term except the first is the term before plus a fixed number.
The fixed number can be positive or negative.
It is called the common difference, d.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A sequence where each term is the previous term plus a fixed number.
The fixed number d added each time: d = next term − this term.

screens.text: Find the common difference d of the arithmetic sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, …
screens.why:
Step 1: d = next term − this term.
Step 2: 5 − 2 = 3, 8 − 5 = 3, 11 − 8 = 3.
Step 3: the gap is the same every time.
So d = 3. (−3 comes from subtracting the wrong way: 2 − 5.)
screens.clue: Subtract a term from the next one.

screens.ask: Find the next term of the arithmetic sequence 9, 6, 3, 0, −3, …: the 6th term is ___
screens.why:
Step 1: d = 6 − 9 = −3 (the terms go down).
Step 2: the 5th term is −3.
Step 3: 6th term = −3 + (−3) = −6.
So the 6th term is −6. (Trap: 0 means −3 − (−3), the wrong direction.)
screens.clue: Find d first. It is negative.

screens.ask: Build an arithmetic sequence from A₁ = 2 and d = −1/2: the 3rd term is ___

screens.text: Spot the arithmetic sequence: which list has the same difference between every pair of terms?
screens.why:
Step 1: 10, 7, 4, 1: gaps −3, −3, −3. Constant, so arithmetic (d = −3).
Step 2: 1, 2, 4, 8: gaps 1, 2, 4. They double: geometric, not arithmetic.
Step 3: 1, 4, 9, 16: gaps 3, 5, 7. Squares, not arithmetic.
Step 4: 1, 1, 2, 3: gaps 0, 1, 1. Fibonacci, not arithmetic.
So the answer is 10, 7, 4, 1, …
screens.clue: Check if the gap stays the same.

screens.ask: Find the missing term in the arithmetic sequence 5, ___, 13, 17. The missing term is
screens.why:
Step 1: 13 and 17 are next to each other, so d = 17 − 13 = 4.
Step 2: the missing term is 5 + 4 = 9.
Check: 9 + 4 = 13 ✓.
So the missing term is 9. (Another way: it is the mean of 5 and 13.)

en.text: To reach the nth term you start at A₁ and add d one time fewer than n: Aₙ = A₁ + (n − 1)d. Put in A₁ and d, then simplify to a rule like 3n − 2. The 31st term needs only n = 31.

am.text: n-ኛውን ተርም ለማግኘት ከ A₁ ተነስተን d ን (n − 1) ጊዜ እንደምራለን፤ Aₙ = A₁ + (n − 1)d።

screens.title: Jump to a far term
screens.ask: 1, 4, 7, 10, … How many times do you add 3 to go from the 1st term to the 31st term?
screens.after:
From term 1 to term 2 is 1 jump; to term 3 is 2 jumps.
So to term 31 there are 31 − 1 = 30 jumps.
A₃₁ = 1 + 30 × 3 = 91.
(31 jumps is the most common slip: it counts the terms, not the gaps.)

screens.title: General term
paras: Each step adds one more d. So the nth term has (n − 1) d's.

screens.title: Explore Aₙ = A₁ + (n − 1)d
screens.ask: Move A₁, d and n. See the nth term.
screens.note: With A₁ = 1, d = 3 and n = 31 you get 91.

screens.title: The dots of 1, 4, 7, 10, 13
screens.ask: Tap the dots. Each step right, the dot rises by d = 3.

points.name: A₅
points.info: 1 + 4(3) = 13: (n − 1) = 4 jumps. The dots lie on a line.

screens.title: Key word
defs: The rule aₙ that gives the nth term.

screens.text: Write the general term of an arithmetic sequence with A₁ = 5 and d = 4.
screens.why:
Step 1: use Aₙ = A₁ + (n − 1)d.
Step 2: Aₙ = 5 + (n − 1)(4).
Step 3: expand: 5 + 4n − 4.
Step 4: collect: Aₙ = 4n + 1.
Check n = 1: 4 + 1 = 5 ✓. (4n + 5 forgets the − 4 from (n − 1).)
screens.clue: Put the numbers into A₁ + (n − 1)d and expand.

screens.text: Write the general term of an arithmetic sequence with A₁ = 10 and d = −5.
screens.why:
Step 1: Aₙ = 10 + (n − 1)(−5).
Step 2: (n − 1)(−5) = −5n + 5. Watch the sign: − × − = +.
Step 3: Aₙ = 10 − 5n + 5 = 15 − 5n.
Check n = 1: 15 − 5 = 10 ✓. (10 − 5n gives A₁ = 5: wrong.)

screens.ask: Use Aₙ = A₁ + (n − 1)d: the 10th term of 10, 6, 2, −2, … is ___
screens.why:
Step 1: A₁ = 10 and d = 6 − 10 = −4.
Step 2: A₁₀ = 10 + (10 − 1)(−4) = 10 + 9(−4).
Step 3: 9 × (−4) = −36, so A₁₀ = 10 − 36 = −26.
So the 10th term is −26. (Trap: 10 jumps gives −30.)

screens.ask: Use Aₙ = A₁ + (n − 1)d with A₁ = 7 and d = 2: A₅₀ = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: n = 50, so n − 1 = 49 jumps.
Step 2: A₅₀ = 7 + 49 × 2.
Step 3: 49 × 2 = 98, and 7 + 98 = 105.
So A₅₀ = 105. (7 + 50 × 2 = 107 is one jump too many.)

screens.text: Counting jumps: true or false? In Aₙ = A₁ + (n − 1)d, the 20th term has 20 jumps of d.
screens.why:
Term 1 has no jumps; term 2 has 1 jump; term 3 has 2.
So term n has n − 1 jumps.
The 20th term has 19 jumps: A₂₀ = A₁ + 19d.
The statement is false.
screens.clue: Count the gaps between term 1 and term 3.

screens.ask: Which term of 5, 8, 11, 14, … equals 50? Term number ___
screens.why:
Step 1: A₁ = 5, d = 3.
Step 2: Aₙ = 5 + (n − 1)3 = 3n + 2.
Step 3: solve 3n + 2 = 50: 3n = 48, n = 16.
Check: 3(16) + 2 = 50 ✓.
So 50 is the 16th term. (n must be a whole number; if not, the number is not a term.)
screens.clue: Write Aₙ as a rule in n, then solve Aₙ = 50.

ideas.name: Finding A₁ and d from two terms

en.text: If you know two terms, write each one as A₁ + (k − 1)d. Subtract the two equations: A₁ cancels and you get d. Then put d back to find A₁. To test whether a rule is arithmetic, work out aₙ₊₁ − aₙ; if no n is left, it is arithmetic.

am.text: ሁለት ተርሞች ከተሰጡ እያንዳንዱን በ A₁ + (k − 1)d መልክ እንጽፋለን። ሁለቱን እኩልታዎች ስንቀንስ A₁ ይጠፋል፤ d እናገኛለን።

screens.title: Between two terms
screens.ask: An arithmetic sequence has A₃ = 10 and A₆ = 1. How many jumps of d are there from A₃ to A₆?
screens.after:
From term 3 to term 6 there are 6 − 3 = 3 jumps.
The 3 jumps change 10 into 1: a change of 1 − 10 = −9.
So each jump is d = −9 ÷ 3 = −3.

screens.title: From A₃ = 10 to A₆ = 1
screens.ask: Tap ▶ for each jump from term 3 to term 6.
screens.after: 3 equal jumps change 10 into 1. So 3d = −9 and d = −3.

screens.title: Is it arithmetic?
paras: If the answer has no n, the difference is constant: arithmetic.
If n is left, the difference changes: not arithmetic.

screens.title: Key word
defs: The fixed number d added each time: d = next term − this term.

screens.text: Find d from two terms: an arithmetic sequence has A₄ = 15 and A₈ = 27. What is d?
screens.why:
Step 1: A₈ = A₁ + 7d and A₄ = A₁ + 3d.
Step 2: subtract: (A₁ + 7d) − (A₁ + 3d) = 27 − 15.
Step 3: 4d = 12, so d = 3.
Short way: term 4 to term 8 is 4 jumps, and 27 − 15 = 12.
(12 is 4d, not d.)

screens.text: Find the general term from two terms: an arithmetic sequence has A₄ = 15 and A₈ = 27.
screens.why:
Step 1: 4 jumps make 27 − 15 = 12, so d = 3.
Step 2: A₁ + 3d = 15, so A₁ = 15 − 9 = 6.
Step 3: Aₙ = 6 + (n − 1)3 = 6 + 3n − 3 = 3n + 3.
Check: A₄ = 12 + 3 = 15 ✓ and A₈ = 24 + 3 = 27 ✓.

screens.ask: Find a term from two given terms: an arithmetic sequence has A₂ = 3 and A₅ = 24. A₁₁ = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: term 2 to term 5 is 3 jumps: 3d = 24 − 3 = 21, so d = 7.
Step 2: A₁ = A₂ − d = 3 − 7 = −4.
Step 3: Aₙ = −4 + 7(n − 1) = 7n − 11.
Step 4: A₁₁ = 77 − 11 = 66.
Check: A₅ = 35 − 11 = 24 ✓.

screens.title: Arithmetic or not?
screens.why:
Step 1: 7n − 3: (7(n + 1) − 3) − (7n − 3) = 7. No n left: arithmetic.
Step 2: 5n − 3: the difference is 5. Arithmetic.
Step 3: n² + n + 1: the difference is 2n + 2. It changes with n: not arithmetic.
Step 4: 3ⁿ: the difference is 3ⁿ⁺¹ − 3ⁿ = 2 × 3ⁿ. It changes: not arithmetic.
Rule: a linear rule pn + q is arithmetic with d = p.
screens.text: Sort each general term: is the sequence arithmetic? Work out aₙ₊₁ − aₙ.

screens.ask: Find d from two terms: an arithmetic sequence has A₅ = 20 and A₁₀ = 0. d = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: term 5 to term 10 is 10 − 5 = 5 jumps.
Step 2: the change is 0 − 20 = −20.
Step 3: 5d = −20, so d = −4.
Check: 20 − 4 − 4 − 4 − 4 − 4 = 0 ✓. (The terms fall, so d must be negative.)

screens.ask: Use two conditions: an arithmetic sequence has A₇ = 2A₃ and A₅ = 18. A₁ = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: A₇ = A₁ + 6d and A₃ = A₁ + 2d.
Step 2: A₁ + 6d = 2(A₁ + 2d) = 2A₁ + 4d, so A₁ = 2d.
Step 3: A₅ = A₁ + 4d = 2d + 4d = 6d = 18, so d = 3.
Step 4: A₁ = 2d = 6.
Check: A₃ = 12, A₇ = 24 = 2 × 12 ✓, A₅ = 18 ✓.
screens.clue: Write both as A₁ + (k − 1)d. The first gives A₁ in terms of d.

en.text: The terms between two given terms of an arithmetic sequence are arithmetic means. One mean between a and b is (a + b)/2. To insert k means between a and b, there are k + 2 terms, so b = a + (k + 1)d.

am.text: በሁለት ቁጥሮች መካከል ያሉት የአሪትሜቲክ ቅደም ተከተል ተርሞች የአሪትሜቲክ አማካዮች ይባላሉ። አንድ አማካይ (a + b)/2 ነው።

screens.title: The middle number
screens.ask: 1, x, 8 is arithmetic. What is x?
screens.after:
In an arithmetic sequence the jumps are equal: x − 1 = 8 − x.
So 2x = 9 and x = 9/2 = 4.5.
It is halfway between 1 and 8: (1 + 8)/2.
(4 is close, but then the jumps 3 and 4 are not equal.)

screens.title: Arithmetic mean
paras: The terms between two given terms are the arithmetic means.
One mean between a and b is (a + b)/2.

screens.title: Four means between 4 and 29
screens.ask: Tap ▶. Five equal hops go from A₁ = 4 to A₆ = 29.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A term between two given terms of an arithmetic sequence.

screens.text: Find the arithmetic mean of 4 and 14 (the number halfway between them).
screens.why:
Step 1: one arithmetic mean between a and b is (a + b)/2.
Step 2: 4 + 14 = 18.
Step 3: 18 ÷ 2 = 9.
Check: 4, 9, 14 has jumps 5 and 5 ✓. (18 is the sum, not the mean.)

screens.title: A₁ = 4, A₆ = 29: terms 2 to 5
steps: 4, A₂, A₃, A₄, A₅, 29 is arithmetic.

screens.ask: Find the arithmetic mean: 3, x, 7 is arithmetic. x = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: equal jumps: x − 3 = 7 − x.
Step 2: 2x = 10.
Step 3: x = 5.
Check: 3, 5, 7 has d = 2 ✓.

screens.text: Insert four arithmetic means between 4 and 14.
screens.why:
Step 1: 4 means plus the 2 ends makes 6 terms: A₁ = 4, A₆ = 14.
Step 2: A₆ = A₁ + 5d, so 14 = 4 + 5d.
Step 3: 5d = 10, d = 2.
Step 4: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. The means are 6, 8, 10, 12.
(5, 7, 9, 11 do not start one jump after 4 with equal steps to 14.)
screens.clue: Four means plus the two ends makes 6 terms.

screens.ask: Find the middle term of an arithmetic sequence: 1/12, 1/x, 1/6 is arithmetic. x = ___
screens.clue: The middle term is the average of the ends.

screens.ask: Insert 5 arithmetic means between −3 and 21. The 3rd mean is ___
screens.why:
Step 1: 5 means + 2 ends = 7 terms: A₁ = −3, A₇ = 21.
Step 2: 21 = −3 + 6d, so 6d = 24 and d = 4.
Step 3: the terms are −3, 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21.
Step 4: the means are 1, 5, 9, 13, 17. The 3rd mean is 9.
(Trap: 5 is the 3rd term, not the 3rd mean.)
screens.clue: k means give k + 2 terms. Find d first.

items.text: For the arithmetic sequence 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, …, give the first term, the third term, d and the 6th term.
items.why:
Step 1: first term = 3; third term = 7.
Step 2: d = 5 − 3 = 2.
Step 3: 6th term = 5th term + d = 11 + 2 = 13.
So: 3, 7, 2, 13.
items.clue: The 6th term is the 5th term + d.

items.ask: Find the next term of the arithmetic sequence 9, 6, 3, 0, −3, …: 6th term = ___
items.why:
Step 1: d = 6 − 9 = −3.
Step 2: 6th term = 5th term + d = −3 + (−3).
Step 3: −3 − 3 = −6.
So the 6th term is −6.

items.ask: Build an arithmetic sequence from A₁ = 1 and d = 5: the 5th term is ___
items.why:
Step 1: A₅ = A₁ + 4d.
Step 2: A₅ = 1 + 4 × 5 = 1 + 20 = 21.
Check by listing: 1, 6, 11, 16, 21 ✓.

items.ask: Build an arithmetic sequence from A₁ = 2 and d = −1/2: the 5th term is ___
items.why:
Step 1: A₅ = A₁ + 4d.
Step 2: 4d = 4 × (−1/2) = −2.
Step 3: A₅ = 2 − 2 = 0.
Check by listing: 2, 3/2, 1, 1/2, 0 ✓.

items.text: Write the general term of an arithmetic sequence with A₁ = 2 and d = 3: Aₙ =
items.why:
Step 1: Aₙ = 2 + (n − 1)3.
Step 2: expand: 2 + 3n − 3.
Step 3: Aₙ = 3n − 1.
Check n = 1: 3 − 1 = 2 ✓. (3n + 2 gives A₁ = 5.)

items.text: Write the general term of an arithmetic sequence with A₁ = 10 and d = −5: Aₙ =

items.ask: Use Aₙ = A₁ + (n − 1)d: the 10th term of 10, 6, 2, −2, … = ___
items.why:
Step 1: A₁ = 10, d = −4.
Step 2: A₁₀ = 10 + 9(−4).
Step 3: 10 − 36 = −26.
So the 10th term is −26.

items.text: Find the general term from two terms: A₄ = 15 and A₈ = 27. Aₙ =
items.why:
Step 1: 4 jumps make 27 − 15 = 12, so d = 3.
Step 2: A₁ = 15 − 3d = 15 − 9 = 6.
Step 3: Aₙ = 6 + 3(n − 1) = 3n + 3.
Check: A₈ = 24 + 3 = 27 ✓.

items.text: Find the general term from two terms: A₅ = 20 and A₁₀ = 0. Aₙ =

items.ask: Find a term from two given terms: A₂ = 3 and A₅ = 24. A₁₁ = ___
items.why:
Step 1: 3 jumps make 24 − 3 = 21, so d = 7.
Step 2: A₁ = 3 − 7 = −4, so Aₙ = 7n − 11.
Step 3: A₁₁ = 77 − 11 = 66.
Short way: A₁₁ = A₅ + 6d = 24 + 42 = 66 ✓.

items.text: Test each general term with aₙ₊₁ − aₙ. Which sequences are arithmetic?
items.why:
Step 1: 7n − 3: difference 7, constant. Arithmetic.
Step 2: 5n − 3: difference 5, constant. Arithmetic.
Step 3: n² + n + 1: difference 2n + 2, it changes. Not arithmetic.
Step 4: 3ⁿ: difference 2 × 3ⁿ, it changes. Not arithmetic.
So 7n − 3 and 5n − 3.
items.clue: Work out aₙ₊₁ − aₙ for each.

items.ask: Find the arithmetic mean: 3, x, 7 is arithmetic. x = ___
items.why:
Step 1: the middle term is halfway: x = (3 + 7)/2.
Step 2: 3 + 7 = 10, and 10 ÷ 2 = 5.
Check: 3, 5, 7 has d = 2 ✓.

items.ask: Find the middle term of an arithmetic sequence: 1/12, 1/x, 1/6 is arithmetic. x = ___
Find the arithmetic mean of 4 and 14 = ___
items.why:
Step 1: add the two numbers: 4 + 14 = 18.
Step 2: halve: 18 ÷ 2 = 9.
Check: 4, 9, 14 has equal jumps of 5 ✓.

items.text: Insert four arithmetic means between 4 and 14.
items.why:
Step 1: 4 means + 2 ends = 6 terms.
Step 2: 14 = 4 + 5d, so d = 2.
Step 3: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14.
The means are 6, 8, 10, 12. (8, 10, 12, 14 includes the end 14.)

test.ask: Use Aₙ = A₁ + (n − 1)d with A₁ = 3 and d = 4: A₂₀ = ___

test.text: Find the common difference of the arithmetic sequence 12, 9, 6, 3, …
test.why:
d = next term − this term.
9 − 12 = −3, 6 − 9 = −3.
The terms fall, so d is negative.
d = −3.

test.ask: Find d from two terms: A₃ = 7 and A₇ = 19. d = ___
test.why:
Term 3 to term 7 is 4 jumps.
The change is 19 − 7 = 12.
4d = 12, so d = 3.

test.text: Which general term is NOT arithmetic? (Test aₙ₊₁ − aₙ.)
test.why:
n² + 1: (n + 1)² + 1 − (n² + 1) = 2n + 1. It depends on n: not arithmetic.
4n − 9: difference 4. 2 − n: difference −1.
(n + 3)/2: difference 1/2.
So n² + 1 is the one that is not arithmetic.

test.ask: Insert 3 arithmetic means between 2 and 18. The middle one is ___
test.why:
3 means + 2 ends = 5 terms.
18 = 2 + 4d, so d = 4.
Terms: 2, 6, 10, 14, 18.
The middle mean is 10. (Check: (2 + 18)/2 = 10 ✓.)

notes.text: The book writes the sequence as Aₙ in 1.2.1 and aₙ elsewhere; lessons keep the book's letters.

screens.title: Solve A₁ + 2d = 10 and A₁ + 5d = 1
steps: Subtract the first from the second: 3d = −9.
Put d back: A₁ + 2(−3) = 10, so A₁ = 16.

screens.text: Solve two equations together: x + 3y = 11 and x + y = 5. What is y?
screens.why:
Step 1: both equations have x once.
Step 2: subtract: (x + 3y) − (x + y) = 11 − 5.
Step 3: 2y = 6, so y = 3.
Step 4: x + 3 = 5, so x = 2.
Check: 2 + 9 = 11 ✓.
screens.clue: Subtract the equations so x disappears.
